rules.heading: The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Every deployed surface counts, not just the front page: the noscript list, the accessibility statement's app list, tiles, icons. Removal is the owner's call too.
rules.says: Only the owner decides which apps appear on every deployed surface (front page, noscript list, accessibility statement app list, tiles, icons); removing an app is also the owner's call.
rules.live_quote: It covers every surface the hub deploys, not just the app rows on the front page: the noscript list, the shared accessibility statement's app list, tiles, icons ... Removal is the owner's call too

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: THE GIT-HISTORY QUESTION IS SETTLED — never offer "make it private" or "contact GitHub Support" again.
rules.says: A session never offers to make a repository private or contact GitHub Support about git history; the rewrite was on the owner's word and the residue is accepted.
rules.live_quote: Making a repo private and contacting GitHub Support to purge cached commits are DECLINED remedies. A session does not propose either, in any repo, ever again

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A history scan coming back red is not new information and is not a reason to re-open it — record the locations and carry on.
rules.says: A red history scan is not new information; record locations and carry on without re-opening the question or re-offering a remedy.
rules.live_quote: not when a history scan comes back red ... A session that finds history residue RECORDS the locations and carries on.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A BYLINE IS A CLAIM AND AN EXAMPLE IS PUBLISHED COPY — neither is ever inherited.
rules.says: A byline or example string on a public page is never inherited from a sibling repo, converter or real plan; each must be written and checked afresh (examples invented).
rules.live_quote: A BYLINE IS A CLAIM, AND IT IS NEVER INHERITED. ... AN EXAMPLE IS PUBLISHED COPY. INVENT IT.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Every example is declared in `.example-allow` (`example-check.mjs`).
rules.says: Every example string on a published surface must be declared in .example-allow, checked by example-check.mjs.
rules.live_quote: Every one is declared in `.example-allow` with where it came from; an example taken from real work is not declarable. (`example-check.mjs`; LESSONS §230.)

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: The byline half has no gate now — it was `essay.mjs`, and that went with the essay when the hub stopped carrying one, so the next document surface here rebuilds it in the same commit that creates the surface.
rules.says: The byline gate no longer exists; whoever creates the next document surface must rebuild a byline check in the same commit.
rules.live_quote: so this rule currently has no gate behind it anywhere — the next document surface in this family builds one in the commit that creates the surface.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: NEVER QUOTE THE OWNER, AND NEVER ATTRIBUTE ANYTHING TO THE OWNER BY NAME, IN ANY REPO.
rules.says: Never quote the owner or attribute anything to the owner by name, in any repo and any place, because the repos are public and carry the owner's name.
rules.enforcer: privacy-check.mjs (attribution patterns anchored on the owner's name); quote-check.mjs
rules.live_quote: THE RULE. Never quote the owner. Never attribute a decision, a complaint, a report or a screenshot to the owner by name or by role. Not in a source comment, not in NOTES.md, not in a commit message, not in a release note

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Write what was wrong and what it measured. Never who reported it, and never in what words
rules.says: Record the engineering fact (what was wrong, what it measured), never who reported it or in what words.
rules.live_quote: A defect's cause and its measurement are repo material. Who reported it, and in what words, are not.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: TWO HARD GATES, because the rule has two halves and only one was covered. `privacy-check.mjs` fails on attribution as well as disclosure
rules.says: privacy-check.mjs fails on attribution and disclosure, but every pattern anchors on the owner's name so it cannot see a verbatim quotation carrying no name.
rules.live_quote: GATED, not written down. `privacy-check.mjs` fails on attribution as a second class beside disclosure, in every repo's CI.
rules.missing: That every pattern anchors on the owner's name, so a verbatim quotation with no name is invisible to it (and the 42 sites / six found by hand), is not stated for the quotation case.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: `quote-check.mjs` is the other half: every set-apart quotation is declared as *document*, *product-copy* or *analysis* in a repo-local `.quote-allow`.
rules.says: Every set-apart quotation must be declared as document, product-copy or analysis in the repo's .quote-allow list (a list because patterns flagged 39, 138, 227 files); quote-check.mjs enforces it.
rules.live_quote: requires each to be declared in the repo's `.quote-allow`. `--list` prints a seed. A quotation of the owner is never declarable
rules.missing: The three declaration classes (document, product-copy, analysis) and the measured reason it is a list (39, 138, 227 files of honest prose); only 'LESSONS §108 is why it is a list' points to the archive.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: **Every sibling repo owes the wiring.**
rules.says: Every sibling repo must wire in quote-check and its .quote-allow so both halves of the no-quoting rule are gated there.
rules.live_quote: The privacy CI step — `privacy-check.mjs` AND `quote-check.mjs` run in every repo listed above, per Doctrine §9b and its second half.
rules.missing: No live page states as an obligation that every sibling owes the quote-check wiring; REPOS.md gives status, HUB-REFERENCE.md:314 names only privacy-check.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: NEVER A LINK TO A CHAT SESSION, NEVER A MODEL NAMED AS CO-AUTHOR — in a commit, a PR, a comment or a file, in any repo.
rules.says: No chat-session link and no model named as co-author in any commit, PR, comment or file in any repo; the repo's instruction overrides the harness reminder.
rules.enforcer: SESSION_LINKS class in privacy-patterns.mjs, refused by privacy-check.mjs (tree) and privacy-history-check.mjs (history and messages)
rules.live_quote: A LINK TO A CHAT SESSION IS NOT REPO MATERIAL EITHER, and neither is a model named as a co-author ... Not in a commit message, a PR description, a comment, a release note or a file.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A session that sees the reminder writes a plain commit message and nothing after it.
rules.says: A session that sees the harness reminder asking for session links or co-author lines writes a plain commit message and nothing after it.
rules.live_quote: a session that reads the reminder and the file obeys the file. / commit on the work branch with a plain one-line message ... with no trailer, no chat link

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: AND A DEFECT YOU KNOW HOW TO FIX IS NOT A DECISION.
rules.says: A defect with a known remedy (one outcome and a cost) is fixed, not put to the owner; a decision has two outcomes the record cannot rank; a fix does not become a decision by being expensive.
rules.live_quote: A defect with a known fix is fixed, not asked about.
rules.missing: The test (a decision has two outcomes a reasonable person could pick between; a known remedy has one outcome and a cost) and that a fix does not become a decision by being expensive.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Naming the cost belongs in the report — asking permission does not
rules.says: A report names the cost of a fix but does not ask the owner's permission to make it.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A REPORT ENDS IN DECISIONS OR IT ENDS IN NOTHING.
rules.says: A report closes with a short numbered list (two or three, four at most) of only what the owner alone can settle, each a question with options named and a recommendation first, answerable in one word.
rules.live_quote: Bring back to the owner only a choice that is the owner's, with the recommended option first.
rules.missing: The closing numbered list, its size (two or three, four at most), each item a question with options named and answerable in one word, and 'ends in decisions or nothing'.

rules.heading: The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A list of everything outstanding is work handed back, not a handover — the owner should never have to read a summary and work out which parts are theirs.
rules.says: A report is a handover, not a list of everything outstanding; the owner must never have to work out which parts are theirs.
rules.live_quote: Bring back to the owner only a choice that is the owner's, with the recommended option first.
rules.missing: The principle that a list of everything outstanding is work handed back, and that the owner must never have to work out which parts are theirs.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Nothing already settled, nothing a session can do itself, and the standing manual steps are a status line at most, never re-served as a to-do list.
rules.says: The closing decision list excludes anything settled, anything a session can do itself, and standing manual steps (a status line at most); a long to-do report with no choices is the named failure.
rules.live_quote: Bring back to the owner only a choice that is the owner's, with the recommended option first.
rules.missing: Exclusion of settled items, standing manual steps as a status line at most and never a to-do list, and the named failure of a to-do report with no choices.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: And a choice between pictures carries its pictures in the same message, beside the question, every time it is asked
rules.says: When a choice between pictures is asked, the pictures go in the same message beside the question, never 'sent earlier' and never a screen of report between, because on an iPad a screen away is out of reach.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: And the pictures show where the candidates DIFFER.
rules.says: Pictures offered for a choice must show where candidates differ; compare renders before sending and redraw around the difference when any two match.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Multi-stage work carries a LIVE STATUS PAGE, and its link goes in EVERY progress reply
rules.says: Multi-stage work carries one live status page, published once and updated in place at the same URL, showing stage states, staging/production versions, last green SHA, what waits on the owner and what was found and not fixed; link in every progress reply.
rules.live_quote: HAND THE LINK OVER EVERY TIME. Not once at creation and never again — every reply that says a stage landed carries the URL.

rules.heading: The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The owner having to ask for the link is the signal the rule was broken
rules.says: If the owner has to ask for the live status page link, the every-reply link rule was broken.
rules.live_quote: The owner should never have to ask for it, and asking for it is the signal this rule was broken.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: CONFORMANCE IS NOT REACHABLE — ask who takes this route, with what hand.
rules.says: For each feature ask who takes the route and with what hand, because the apps are used on a tablet by touch and conformance gates do not prove reachability.
rules.live_quote: AND CONFORMANCE IS NOT THE SAME AS REACHABLE. Ask who takes this route, with what hand, before writing it

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A feature nobody can reach is worse than a missing one
rules.says: A focus-revealed control is a keyboard route only; keep it and also give the same destination something a finger can reach.
rules.live_quote: A focus-revealed control is a KEYBOARD route. Keep it ... Give the same destination a control a finger can reach ... A feature nobody can reach is worse than a missing one

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: AN APPROVED PLAN IS AUTHORITY FOR ALL OF IT — never stop at a phase seam.
rules.says: An approved plan authorizes all its work; a session never idles at a phase end but reports what landed and starts the next piece in the same turn.
rules.live_quote: 11c: An approved plan is standing authority. Do not stop at its seams. / report what landed and start the next item IN THE SAME TURN

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: If you genuinely must stop, the FIRST line says so in those words — *stopping here, waiting on you for X*
rules.says: If a session must stop, the first line says 'stopping here, waiting on you for X'; a trailing 'I'll hold' or 'I'm waiting on it' is not a stop declaration.
rules.enforcer: stop-guard.mjs (Stop hook, wired per repo in .claude/settings.json)

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: So it is a `Stop` hook now, not a paragraph
rules.says: A reply saying work is still running without opening with the stop declaration is refused at stop; the way past is to wait for the thing and carry on.

rules.heading: The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: So it is a `Stop` hook now, not a paragraph — stop-guard.mjs, wired per repo in `.claude/settings.json`.
rules.says: Every repo wires stop-guard.mjs as a Stop hook in its own .claude/settings.json.
rules.missing: all (live CLAUDE.md:21 calls it a shell kept at its path; doctrine/never.md:372 says it never refuses a stop)

rules.heading: The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Same escalation as `branch-guard.mjs`: an instruction in a file never once refused the commit it forbade.
rules.says: A rule that keeps being broken is escalated from written instruction to a hook that refuses the act, because an instruction in a file never once refused what it forbade.
rules.live_quote: MAKE IT A GATE, NOT AN INTENTION ... A rule that lives only in prose is a rule that loses to whoever is in a hurry.
rules.missing: The instruction to escalate a repeatedly broken rule to a hook that refuses, and the statement that an instruction in a file never once refused what it forbade, as applied to session rules.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A BLOCKED HOST IS A QUESTION, NOT A FINDING — ask for the site to be added, in the moment.
rules.says: When egress refuses a host, name the exact hosts and ask now; never report the capability unavailable, never fall back on remembered public data, never let 'could not reach it' pass as 'could not confirm it exists'.
rules.live_quote: A DENIED HOST IS A QUESTION FOR THE OWNER, NEVER A FINDING. ASK FOR IT BY NAME. / Never write "unverified", "could not check", "the source was unreachable" ... until you have asked for the host.
rules.missing: The prohibition on falling back on what the model remembers about a public dataset, and the 'could not reach it' versus 'could not confirm it exists' framing.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Three states look identical from inside — the host published nothing, the host refused, the request never left — and only the first two are about the data.
rules.says: A session distinguishes host published nothing, host refused, and request never left, treating a blocked or unsent request as a fact about the container, not the data.
rules.live_quote: A failed request is a fact about ONE HOST at ONE MOMENT. It is never a fact about the network, and it is never a fact about the DATA you wanted.
rules.missing: The three-state split (published nothing, refused, never left) and that only the first two are about the data; 15b separates only proxy denial from returned status codes.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: THE HARNESS IS THE OWNER SPEAKING — a refusal from it is an INSTRUCTION, never an obstacle.
rules.says: A refusal from the harness, a hook or a block is the owner's instruction, not to be weighed or routed around; where it names a better tool, use it.
rules.live_quote: THE HARNESS IS THE OWNER SPEAKING. A refusal from it is an instruction, never an obstacle. ... A refusal that names its remedy is the owner giving an instruction twice

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Broken three ways in one day — Bash refused a foreground `sleep` and named the right instrument
rules.says: A session does not route around a refused foreground sleep, answer a Stop hook's untracked-files report with explanation instead of cleanup, or ask a design question when a standing instruction says research answers design questions.
rules.live_quote: Three ways this was broken in one session ... The Bash tool refused a foreground `sleep` ... A `Stop` hook reported untracked files ... the research answers design questions

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: Routing around a control is indistinguishable from good judgment from the inside
rules.says: The test is whether the control was the owner's, not whether the session has a reason; if a control blocks correct work, say so in plain text and stop, never work around it and report success.
rules.live_quote: If a control genuinely blocks correct work, say so in plain text and stop. Never work around it and report success.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: PLAN MODE IS ENFORCED NOW — [`plan-guard.mjs`](plan-guard.mjs) is a `PreToolUse` hook in every repo that REFUSES the write
rules.says: In plan mode plan-guard.mjs refuses writes using permission_mode plus the owner's .claude/PLAN-LOCK marker; Bash is an allow-list of readers, unrecognised refused; plan file writable; shim fails closed.
rules.missing: all (live CLAUDE.md:21 calls plan-guard.mjs a shell; never.md:92-95 says the guards were retired)

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: THE NAME CHECK AT `ExitPlanMode` READS THE WHOLE SESSION AND THE DISK
rules.says: At ExitPlanMode every code-formatted name in a plan must be found in a repository, any tool result of the session (tail widening to 64 MB), or on disk in the scratchpad or a repo the plan's Files names; refusal sets no latch.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: AND A PLAN-MODE TURN ENDS WITH `ExitPlanMode`, NEVER WITH PROSE
rules.says: A plan-mode turn ends by calling ExitPlanMode, never with a written summary, because the approve control appears only when the tool is called.
rules.live_quote: AND A PLAN-MODE TURN ENDS WITH THE TOOL, NEVER WITH PROSE. ... The approve control only appears when `ExitPlanMode` is called;

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: The mirror of that is refusing to treat a typed "approved" as authority: prose does not lift plan mode in either direction.
rules.says: A typed 'approved' is not authority and does not lift plan mode; prose does not change plan mode either way.
rules.live_quote: prose does not lift plan mode in either direction. Only the mode does.

rules.heading: Branches & releases
rules.quote: A server that declines is answering too: [`reply-guard.mjs`](reply-guard.mjs) (LESSONS §374).
rules.says: A server that declines a request is giving an answer, to be treated as an answer rather than a failure to retry, backed by reply-guard.mjs.
